input.description: Find render env handling in boot script

content.text:
I made no edits to the integration tree — the failure is not the wave's.

**Diagnosis.** All three failing sims (`test_sandbox_boot.mjs`, `test_sandbox_boot_state_exams.mjs`, `test_sandbox_boot_effort.mjs`) fail on the same assertion: the engine's argv carries `TINYAPP_RENDER_URL=https://browser-run.int.exe.xyz/...` where the tests expect the empty `TINYAPP_RENDER_URL=`. The rig's `bootEnv` in `fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs` does not set `FLEET_RENDER_ENV`, so a bare boot falls back to the literal `/etc/fleet/render.env` (`fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:72`, sourced at `:700`) — and **this sandbox host has that file**, root-owned and populated with the real edge address. The rig is not hermetic against the production fallback path; the three sims only pass on a box whose setup never installed it.

**Why it isn't a composition seam.** None of the four files this wave touched go near the render block: `sandbox-boot.sh`'s diff is comment text plus the fold-attempt ceiling; the helper diff adds the `date` clock stub and the optional `script` parameter to `boot`/`bootAsync`. The three failing test files are untouched by the wave. I confirmed this empirically rather than by inspection: I built a throwaway copy of the tree, reset the four modified files to `HEAD` content, and ran `node fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot.mjs` there — it fails with the identical single assertion. (The copy has been deleted; no git state was mutated and no manifest or lockfile changed in this wave, so no install applied.)

**What would fix it** — out of reconcile's scope, since it means rewriting a prior wave's assertions: default `FLEET_RENDER_ENV` in `bootEnv` to a per-home path that does not exist (the `...env` spread already lets the planted cases override it), and rewrite leg (a)'s precondition at `test_sandbox_boot_state_exams.mjs:286` to assert *that* path is absent instead of `/etc/fleet/render.env`.
